One place to find, control, and resume.

From a file you just downloaded to a quieter PC, start with what you want to do.

Illustrative examples of Scout. These previews do not search your PC or run commands.

Find the file. Even when the name escapes you.

Search by name, folder, type, or activity. Scout can distinguish when a file was modified, downloaded, or opened, using the records available on your PC.

“the pdf I just downloaded”

Optional Chrome or Edge integration provides completed-download evidence. Without it, Scout labels file-arrival estimates so you can tell the difference.

Try “files I opened this morning.” Matches depend on recorded Windows Recent Items or successful Scout launches.

Small tasks. Fewer steps.

Type a supported command, review the action, and press Enter. Everyday controls are right beside your files and apps.

  • wifi offTurn Wi-Fi off
  • bluetooth offTurn Bluetooth off
  • muteMute your sound
  • volume upRaise output volume
  • brightness downLower display brightness
  • darkToggle light / dark appearance
  • lock screenLock your Windows session

Also turn Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on, unmute, and lower volume. Brightness controls require a supported integrated display; Windows policies and hardware can limit controls.

Bring the pieces of your work together.

Ask for “latest three files in Downloads.” Review the group, choose its members, and open them together.

Save a workspace with the files, apps, and links you use for a project. Search its name when you want to return to that set.

Workspaces reopen saved items. They do not restore unsaved document edits or an app’s previous window layout.

Your PC.
Your choices.

Your index, pins, workspaces, and launch history stay on your PC. Choose the folders Scout searches and the optional features you enable.

Core search and system commands work without optional AI. Every launch or command requires Enter or an explicit Open action.

Browser history is optional
Enable Chrome and Edge separately to include visited links and completed downloads. Scout does not read incognito data or cookies.
Content search is optional
Supported document and source text is indexed only in selected folders. Extracted body text stays local and is never sent to the model. Turning content search off clears its index.
Local AI is optional
The runtime and model are separate downloads. Inference runs on your PC after setup. Performance depends on your hardware; descriptive matches can be imperfect.

A few things to know

How do I install, open, and quit Scout?

Run Scout-Setup.exe and follow the prompts. Setup installs for your account without admin access, adds Scout to Start, and opens it when finished.

Press Ctrl + Alt + Space to open the panel. Closing the panel leaves Scout in the notification area. Press Ctrl + Q or choose Quit to exit.

Can I use a portable version?

Download the portable ZIP, extract the entire archive, and run Scout.exe. It uses the same local settings storage as the installer. ZIP checksum

Do I need AI or a Copilot+ PC?

No. Core search, supported folder and activity queries, calculations, system commands, and workspaces work without optional AI on Windows 11 x64. Local AI is off by default and requires separate runtime and model downloads with several GB of storage.

CPU inference is available but can be slow on ordinary laptops. CUDA requires a supported NVIDIA GPU. AI helps refine candidates; it does not guarantee a match or read document body text.

What can content search and previews read?

Optional content indexing covers supported text/source, Office, and OpenDocument files in selected folders. PDF body text and OCR are not indexed. Files larger than 16 MiB are skipped, and extraction is limited to 64,000 characters per file.

PDF page previews are available separately. Office and OpenDocument previews show text rather than the full application layout.

Will every PC control work on my device?

Radio, sound, and display controls depend on Windows policy, drivers, and hardware support. Scout reports failures. Brightness commands target supported integrated displays; external monitors commonly do not support them.

The dark command toggles appearance. Notification commands open Windows notification settings. Commands run only when you explicitly choose them.

How do I update or uninstall?

Updates are manual. Quit Scout, then run the newer installer. For a portable copy, replace the extracted application folder with the newer ZIP’s contents.

Uninstall through Start or Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps. Settings and workspaces remain in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Scout for a later reinstall. Read the beta 2 release notes.
